newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BUSINESS WELCOMES GOVT TAX REFORM PLANS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BUSINESS WELCOMES GOVT TAX REFORM PLANS.

text.p: The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry welcomed on Wednesday the government's accelerated move towards tax reform and the establishment of an internal task force to examine options.

"The government has recognised that the current taxation system is holding back our industries' ability to compete through excessive reliance on taxing business inputs, complexity and massive compliance costs," chief executive Mark Paterson said in a statement.
Paterson said employment was also affected because of high marginal income tax rates at relatively low levels of income.
"The Prime Minister's announcement that there will be no overall increase in taxation collection is a sensible approach," Paterson said.
"His emphasis on a broad-based simplified indirect tax system ... will make an important contribution to a tax system better able to attract investment, create jobs and promote exports."
Earlier on Wednesday, Prime Minister John Howard pledged to reform Australia's complex taxation system, promising to cut income taxes and to declare the government's plans ahead of the next election.
Howard also announced that the government would set up a tax reform task force.

The Liberal-National coalition has long favoured a tax on consumption of goods and services, but abandoned that policy in its successful 1996 election campaign after losing what was regarded as an unloseable election in 1993 with such a policy.
Business and community groups have stepped up their calls for reforms to Australia's tax system, with its near 50 percent top income tax and a complex and patchy range of indirect taxes.
"Anybody who has the national economic interest at heart knows that we cannot go into the 21st century with our existing taxation system," Howard told reporters earlier on Wednesday.
